title: Kinetic Headroom Synthesizer: hybrid predictive-slew autoscaler for Dedicated fleets
creator: Ari Chen
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput with tight latency SLOs while minimizing over-provisioning and avoiding noisy, destabilizing scale events. Existing autoscalers either react too late (simple thresholding) or are aggressively predictive but unsafe under sudden load shifts.

Goal: Build the 'Kinetic Headroom Synthesizer' (KHS) — an autoscaling policy engine that synthesizes multiple target metrics into a single scale intent, using a hybrid predictive + kinetic-slew algorithm and explicit safety limits. KHS should: 1) support per-tenant and per-fleet targets; 2) combine throughput, p95 latency, GPU occupancy, and KV cache hit signals; 3) expose config knobs for headroom crediting, burst windows, and cooldown/rollback; 4) surface observability and explainability for each scale decision.

Design summary: KHS composes three layers:
- Target estimator: converts telemetry (tokens/s, req/s, p95, occupancy, kv_hit) into a short-term demand curve (percentile forecast + uncertainty band). Uses lightweight time-series forecasting (exponential smoothing + quantile regressors) tuned for low compute and quick adaption.
- Kinetic synthesizer: translates the demand curve into an adjusted headroom requirement using a kinetic model (mass/inertia analogy). The kinetic model enforces a maximum slew-rate (scale up/down speed) and incorporates a credit balance (burst budget) that allows short-lived violations without triggering long-lived provisioning.
- Safety envelope & policy guards: applies hard limits (min/max fleet capacity), thermal/placement constraints, and a rollback window. Safety checks include: occupancy floor (to avoid OOM/oversubscription), P95 backstop (if p95 exceeds X ms after scale, trigger rollback), and burst debt cap (prevent repeated bursts that drain credits).

Config schema example (stringified YAML for readability):

"""
policy_kind: kinetic_headroom_synthesizer
targets:
  - name: tokens_per_sec
    weight: 0.5
  - name: p95_latency_ms
    weight: 0.3
  - name: gpu_occupancy
    weight: 0.15
  - name: kv_hit_rate
    weight: 0.05
predictor:
  method: exp_smoothing_quantile
  horizon_seconds: 60
  quantile: 0.9
kinetic:
  max_slew_up_percent_per_min: 40
  max_slew_down_percent_per_min: 25
  burst_credit_seconds: 300
  recovery_window_seconds: 120
safety_envelope:
  min_capacity_replicas: 2
  max_capacity_replicas: 120
  p95_backstop_ms: 350
  occupancy_max_percent: 95
  rollback_grace_seconds: 90
observability:
  explain_rate: 1m
  dashboard_link: "https://confluence.redwood/company/dedicated/khs-dashboard"
"""

Why this is different: KHS is tuned for LLM inference workloads where request inter-arrival distributions are bursty and token-generation makes per-request cost non-linear. Instead of a single metric-driven autoscaler, KHS fuses multiple orthogonal signals and explicitly models inertia and temporary credit to reduce oscillation while still allowing short bursts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature flag gated rollout for Dedicated tenants.
- Unit and e2e tests for predictor + kinetic synthesizer.
- Dashboard with per-decision explanation (signal weights, predicted demand, applied slew, credit delta).
- Canary run on the staging Dedicated pool with synthetic burst profiles; meet latency SLOs (p95 <= configured backstop) and demonstrate <=10% extra capacity over current baseline for a set of representative workloads.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Telemetry normalizer service changes (thin adapter to emit standardized signals). Owner: telemetry infra.
2) Implement predictor module as a pluggable library in runtime control plane. Owner: serving runtime team.
3) Implement kinetic synthesizer + credit accounting in autoscaler service; include REST config API and validation. Owner: autoscaler team.
4) Safety envelope enforcement integrated with capacity allocator and placement. Owner: capacity allocator.
5) Observability: decision events, explain traces, dashboard panels. Owner: console team.
6) Canary + runbook for rollback. Owner: SRE.

Open questions: 
- What quantiles are best for different customer classes (startup vs enterprise)? (Action: PM to interview top 5 Dedicated customers).
- What budget model for burst credits per-tenant vs per-fleet is fair and simplest to bill? (Action: Finance + Product workshop).
- Should the predictor allow customer-supplied demand hints (ingestion of scheduled jobs)?
